claims.statement: Discovery landing metadata covers FPT/GHEC/GHES and organizes get-started, publication/management and registry categories with quickstart/overview links, nine recommended paths and four child sections. These lists are navigation, not proof every linked page is reviewed or every registry enabled.

Introductory safe publishing/consumption and Actions automation language expresses purpose, not tested safety, rights clearance or authority to share publicly. Repository-adjacent packages can have separate visibility and access.

Learning index lists eight permission/access/link/publish/view/install/delete-restore child pages and redirects across FPT/GHEC/GHES. Deletion is described as special circumstances, not a universal lifecycle instruction; release-stage include is comment-only. Navigation does not prove linked-file completeness.

Actions overview resolves the packaging reusable: CI packaging after build/test may create runnable/deployable artifacts for review/manual tests, e.g. JAR or container. An artifact download is not safe execution, successful functional testing or package-registry publication evidence.

Overview distinguishes CI artifact uploads from registry publication and offers default-branch pushes or release creation as possible publication events. These are choices/examples, not unconditional per-push publishing policy, deployment approval or guaranteed latest-build access.

Example-workflow page links package workflow and Node/Docker/Maven/Gradle Actions guides across FPT/GHEC/GHES. No executable workflow is authored here; outbound references remain separate artifacts and examples do not establish immutable pins, credentials, behavior or authority.

Workflow index lists three publication/install, example and overview children for FPT/GHEC/GHES. Its safe build/test/deploy introduction is not verified enforcement or permission to deploy; release-stage reusable is only comment data.

Registry index lists eight Container/Docker/RubyGems/npm/Maven/Gradle/NuGet/migration children plus redirects across FPT/GHEC/GHES. Supported-registry introduction is qualified by feature/instance/version limits in child guides; child listing is not full corpus review or runtime availability, and release-stage include is comment-only.
